honest_headline: REFUTED. The signed mr-memory-detector-arl-degradation-v1 receipt (folded into the consolidated ARL-characterization KPI v2 and restated in mission.md) asserts MRbar/d2(2) is 'the estimator the Individuals chart actually defaults to (operating estimator)' and S/c4(m) is merely an 'upper bound, not the operating estimator'. Direct inspection of the live, checked amphora-formulation-capabilities/src/lib.rs::audit_process_qc function -- cross-confirmed by the module's own bit-exact independent-recompute Phase-0 gate (which already labels the quantity 'sample stdev') and by a fresh cargo-executed probe on this exact checkout -- shows the runtime computes plain (uncorrected) sample standard deviation over the full baseline window: no moving range is ever computed. This tracks the S/c4 family (raw_S vs S/c4 diverges only -1.3% on a drifting baseline) and diverges sharply from MRbar/d2 (+246% on the same input) -- the exact opposite of the attacked receipt's classification. The consequence is real, not cosmetic: on a physically plausible drifting baseline, a genuine out-of-control shift that a correctly MRbar/d2-attributed 3-sigma limit would flag is missed by all three live detectors (Shewhart, EWMA, CUSUM) because the runtime's actual raw-S estimate inflates under baseline drift. No receipt on file has ever characterized ARL/false-alarm/recall degradation under the estimator the runtime actually uses (raw, uncorrected sample S); the entire consolidated ARL-characterization KPI v2 has, since its first fire, characterized an estimator (MRbar/d2) the deployed code does not implement.

independent_python_rederivation.interpretation: On the module's own benign closed-form sawtooth fixture, raw S, S/c4, and MRbar/d2 happen to sit within ~11% of one another -- close enough that the misattribution was easy to miss and never previously exercised. Under a physically realistic drifting baseline (a plausible pilot-onboarding warm-up transient, not a contrived edge case), raw S diverges from MRbar/d2 by 246%, while diverging from S/c4 by only -1.3% -- i.e. the runtime's ACTUAL estimator tracks the S/c4 family (as expected, since raw S and S/c4 are both full-sample-variance-based, differing only by a deterministic bias correction) and does NOT track MRbar/d2 at all. This is the opposite of the attacked receipt's classification, which treats S/c4 as the sidelined 'upper bound' and MRbar/d2 as the real operating estimator.

scenario_b_drift_warmup_physically_reali.description: Linear ramp of total range 2.0 across the 20 baseline observations (e.g. a cure-oven or dispense-head warm-up during pilot onboarding) with the same local wiggle superimposed as scenario A. Finite, uniquely and strictly sequenced, non-empty batch ids: passes every existing fail-closed gate in audit_process_qc (time-ordering, contamination, missingness).

This is a directly demonstrated, real (cargo-executed, not simulated) consequence of the misattribution, not merely a labeling nitpick.

refutation_criterion_applied: The attacked field is a factual claim about which sigma estimator the live, checked amphora-process-qc-twin implementation uses: 'the estimator the Individuals chart actually defaults to'. This is refuted if direct inspection of the live, checked source (amphora-formulation-capabilities/src/lib.rs::audit_process_qc, the exact function mission.md cites as 'the live checked implementation') shows the runtime computes a different estimator, AND real (not simulated) execution of that function confirms the mismatch has operational consequence (a genuine out-of-control shift, flaggable under the claimed estimator's control limits, is missed under the runtime's actual limits). Both occurred.

source_ground_truth.formula_classification: Bessel-corrected (n-1) sample variance of the full baseline window, square-rooted. This is the plain (uncorrected-by-c4) sample standard deviation S. It is computed directly from squared deviations about the baseline mean; the function contains no consecutive-difference (moving-range) computation anywhere, and no division by a c4(n) or d2(2) unbiasing constant.
